#1493. Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4

“A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose said. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that showed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

"Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y

"That's a big moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39

Cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young said on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose big players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”

Fair play to anyone who retained Brobbey in their Fantasy Football teams this week...

4 - Brian Brobbey is the fourth player in Premier League history to score a hat-trick against the side starting the day top of the table, after Robbie Fowler v Aston Villa in November 1998, Dirk Kuyt v Man Utd in March 2011, and Romelu Lukaku v Man Utd in May 2013.Unstoppable. pic.twitter.com/vygVYazIQD

Maresca’s side maintain their immaculate record, but boy were they made to work for it this afternoon.

Sunderland are still 5-3 down but have not given up the ghost. Surely the best match of the season so far?

It ends goalless at Elland Road after Mitchell’s goal was disallowed for offside. Kamada went close to breaking the deadlock in the final stages...

Daichi Kamada can't guide his header on target! ❌ pic.twitter.com/AgKM6Q9apq

Bournemouth lose at the Vitality for the first time in 13 matches as Iraola makes a winning return to the South Coast. Liverpool were hardly impressive, but to their credit they managed the final stages of this match with a minimum of fuss.

Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium with a win! ✅ pic.twitter.com/FSgvE6EGFB

Bournemouth are awarded a corner but Brooks’ delivery goes straight into the inviting gloves of Alisson.

Koumas pressures Petrovic, but the goalkeeper shows off some tidy footwork to escape the danger.

Bournemouth cannot get out though, and Petrovic is forced into a routine save off Koumas moments later.

Bournemouth win a free-kick in a dangerous position after a handball, but Scott cannot get his strike up and down fast enough and it sails over.

Haaland gets in on the act, but only after a VAR check. That should be that...

Erling Haaland has now scored against all 25 teams he has faced in the Premier League ✅⚽ pic.twitter.com/X9uqcrgbwk

Araujo gets his pocket picked in the corner but Jebbison cannot compose himself and blasts his cross off the other side of the pitch.

Liverpool go the other way and win a corner, but Mac Allister puts too much air on his delivery and it is easily dealt with.

Rayan wins a free-kick as he holds off Kerkez on the halfway line. Bournemouth then switch play to the far side but Truffert’s speculative effort flies well over the bar.

Nyoni shows off his composure on the ball, playing simple passes on the half-turn to keep play flowing. The midfield area is quite congested, which suits Liverpool at this point in the game.

Liverpool are baiting Bournemouth’s press in an attempt to play around their front line. They are doing a good job at holding on to the ball and frustrating their opponents, for now.

Gravenberch and Koumas are on for Gakpo and Isak.

Brooks has brought some energy to Bournemouth’s forays down the left. He attempts to slip a ball into the left channel but Nyoni is wise to it and positions himself perfectly to cut it out.

Liverpool have dropped deep and Bournemouth wait patiently for an opening. They eventually find Tavernier in the left half-space but his cross flies over everyone.

That is his last contribution to the match as Rose rings the changes: Tavernier, Smith and Christie make way for Brooks, Jebbison and Cook.

Truffert spins in a teasing ball from the left but Jacquet does well to flick the ball away from the danger zone.

Wirtz and Barcola make way for Nyoni and Munoz. Quiet afternoon from both of the outgoing players.

A stunning block from Hill prevents Isak pulling trigger as he looked to have the goal in his sights.

Truffert clears the resulting corner to safety.

Isak is concentrating his efforts in more central areas and here he almost gets played in behind but the ball just runs away from him. Better.

Worth mentioning that Jacquet has been fantastic in all phases of the game. Plenty of advanced regains and tidy passes forward.

It’s raining goals in Manchester and no prizes for guessing who has scored for Sunderland. Brobbey has his hat-trick.

Brobbey has his hat-trick and the look on Enzo Maresca’s face as he assesses the defending from his team. They’ve been great pouring forward, less so trying to stymie Sunderand’s attack. But this is one of those games where you just sit back and enjoy the unfolding drama. It’s been so good from both teams.

Semenyo gets his second goal of the afternoon to extend the league leaders’ advantage.

Chance! Jacquet jumps and wins the ball well inside Bournemouth’s half and his intervention sends the ball into Isak’s path. The forward just drags his effort wide and turns out he was in an offside postion anyhow.

What an afternoon this is turning out to be. There have been more slices than on an erratic day on the local municipal golf course and Ronald Araujo is the latest to be afflicted by the condition. None of that will matter to Andoni Iraola, though, as Alexander Isak’s fourth goal in four Premier League games has given Liverpool a huge advantage. They haven’t played with fluency but the breakthrough was significant.

Isak opens the scoring at the Vitality, finally getting into the box and sweeping in from close range. So much credit has to go to Gakpo who tiptoes past two Bournemouth defenders by the touchline before spearing a cross infield, and while he may not be attributed with the assist owing to a touch off Wirtz, his delivery makes it all the way through to Isak who taps in.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4

Adams has been superb as one of Bournemouth’s two midfield sentries. Kerkez looks to have been played into the left channel but the American swoops in and shields the ball out of play before staring down his Hungarian opponent.

Mitchell thinks he’s given the visitors the lead but his goal is ruled out for offside.

Tyrick Mitchell's opener is disallowed for an offside in the build up! ❌ pic.twitter.com/7y975TxaUj

Liverpool give up possession in Bournemouth’s half and Christie strides forward releasing Rayan before continuing his run to the near post. The Brazilian picks out his team-mate but Christie gets too strong a contact on the ball and the ball sails wide.

Truffert passes the ball straight to Gakpo inside his own box but Adams is on the scene in a flash and snaps into a tackle and takes the ball away from the Liverpool forward.

The second has already settled into a holding pattern, with neither side creating much. Isak makes a run down the right hand side and, with players loaded in the box, he blasts the ball high into the sky and beyond his team-mates. That pretty much sums things up.

Wirtz has given the ball away twice in the first minute of the second half. Carragher is on Sky Sports commentary duties and he says he’s surprised to see him back out on the pitch.

Szoboszlai concedes a foul on the far side but the subsequent delivery is too heavy and sails over everyone.

No half-time changes from either manager.

Isak’s first-half heatmap makes for interesting reading. The good news, for Liverpool fans, is that he’s stationed himself predominantly in the final third. The bad news... those positions have been everywhere but the box.

Big chance missed from Haaland of all people to make it 4-2 to City in what has been a pulsating, spell-binding first 45 minutes. It’s fast, furious and a helluva lot of fun to watch. Brilliant from Ndiaye to tee up Haaland who shoots wide of a post. A game for attackers shall we say ...

There are significant advantages to having a goalkeeper who is 6ft 5in with long arms and massive hands. Not a pretty half from the returning Iraola’s side, who will need to be much better in the second period to challenge for the three points.

Bournemouth have dropped points late on in a number of matches this season and will perhaps rue not being able to capitalise on their early advantage.

City are in front. Again. Semenyo this time, he fires the ball beyond Roefs having collected a loose ball int he box.

Antoine Semenyo gets his first goal of the season! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/1n2W5Cyxz0

A relatively slick Liverpool move sees the ball worked out to Araujo on the right who has minded to bomb on with increasing frequency, and while he’s able to win a corner, Szoboszlai’s delivery is cleared with a minimum of fuss.

Iraola came into this game saying that his side held an advantage having played two days earlier than Bournemouth in midweek. You would never have guessed it from what we have witnessed here today.

And right on cue, a frustrated Isak attempts a specultative effort from range which sails high and wide.

Sunderland fans sing “F--- VAR” and City fans boo the delay while they both awaited the verdict, which has now gone Sunderland’s way

So, this is not a rush to make a sweeping criticism, it’s simply an observation. But Liverpool fans will be looking at Bradley Barcola and  waiting to see that first burst, that moment of electricity, that has showed why they bought him. It’s like you look for a touch, a pass, a moment of skill. He’s just had a shot saved but it all seems very tentative for him at the moment. And that is what he needs - a moment.

Jacquet does brilliantly to close down Christie as the Scot was stealing into the box and looking to pull the trigger.

Chances! Barcola forces Petrovic into an awkward-looking save, before follow-up efforts from Wirtz and Gakpo are charged down.

Mac Allister is fouled 25 yards out moments later and Szoboszlai gets another go. Here, he drags his effort just wide.

It’s all happening at the Etihad. Cherki restores City’s lead with his third Premier League goal of the season.

It’s a great finish from Cherki to put City back in front but it doesn’t happen if Ndiaye is quick to read Danso’s risky pass and win possession. Sharp as a button in that moment.

Rayan Cherki puts Manchester City back in front! 💫 pic.twitter.com/PP4MAV9kw3

A really poor piece of defending from Kerkez gives Bournemouth a free-kick out on the right. Tavernier spins in an inswinger but Van Dijk heads clear. Truffert launches another assault on Liverpool’s box off the second phase but Alisson is wise to it and gathers.

It appears that Liverpool are beginning to settle, they take the opportunity to circulate the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure, waiting for the right moment to pounce. The final pass is poor, though, and Araujo through-pass goes all the way through to Petrovic. It was aimed at Isak ...I think.

Some signs of life from Liverpool, as they create a substantial overload down their left, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Barcola and Isak meeting on that flank. Liverpool will not be pleased with their start to this match. They’ve struggled to string more than three passes together without ceding possession and Isak has cut an isolated figure up top.

First time that Bournemouth have gone through the gears and the move ends with Alisson Becker saving brilliantly from Evanilson. It’s a funny stadium, here, as it can be quiet then all of a sudden a tempest whips up and you can sense the mood changing. Jacquet gives away a needless foul on the near side but Scott’s delivery goes straight into Alisson’s hands. The Brazilian’s throw out is poor, though, and Scott darts into Liverpool’s box, just unable to pick out a team-mate.

Barcola is presented with green grass to run into, but just as he builds a head of steam Hill comes across in a flash and snuffs out the foray forward.

Woah, Brobbey responds immediately, stealing in between City defenders before slotting past Donnarumma.

Instant response from Sunderland as Brian Brobbey equalises! 💥 pic.twitter.com/et6AHGPAbl

Enzo Fernandez opens the scoring at the Etihad with a direct free-kick from out wide. Really poor from Roefs who was caught napping. That’s Fernandez’s first City goal.

Wirtz earns a free-kick just outside the D. Bournemouth feel aggrieved as there looked to have been an earlier foul on Scott and to make matters worse Szoboszlai is standing over the ball.

His effort leaves Petrovic rooted to the spot but the ball veers just wide of the mark.

Evanilson’s willingness to drop deep is asking questions of Liverpool’s centre-backs. Do they follow him and risk disrupting their backline coverage?

The hosts attempt to work a short corner routine but Truffert’s eventual through-ball is too strong and the ball rolls out for a Liverpool goal-kick.

This wouldn’t go down as a fixture you would circle for being noteworthy but make no mistake this is a huge afternoon for Liverpool. They have had some days at the Vitality Stadium in recent years and last season’s defeat put a huge dent in Arne Slot’s hopes of trying to find a revival. It’s also a big test for Bournemouth, coming down from the euphoria of beating Real Sociedad. Let’s see how it all transpires.

Evanilson makes a smart run into the right channel and while Jacquet gets his foot on the ball he’s instantly smothered by Scott and the ball goes out for a Liverpool goal-kick. A sign of how high both sides will be willing to jump in search of the ball.

Both sides will look to force mistakes out of the other and Szoboszlai is able to pick Adams’ pocket on the halfway line. He offloads to Araujo who runs into a cul de sac down the right flank.

We are under way at the Vitality. Bournemouth are in their customary black-and-red home shirts kicking from right to left and Liverpool are in their white away kit and red shorts.

The players have emerged from the tunnel, Van Dijk and Smith at the front of the lines. A few pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere but one thing missing is the accidental sitting in the wrong dugout from the returning Iraola. He knows where he’s going.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

#1492. Como: Andrea Le Borgne, the next Frenchman that Fabregas could blow up

For the French public, last year’s U20 World Cup was an opportunity to discover new faces, still largely unknown. The French coach, Bernard Diomède, had to show ingenuity when putting together his group, after having suffered no less than 48 refusals from clubs (the tournament was not included in the FIFA calendar of dates). Certain profiles, not necessarily scheduled to be there at the start, took this opportunity to show themselves and advance to the semi-final.

We think, for example, of Gady Beyuku, whose career we are telling you about, or of Andrea Le Borgne, transferred to Como a few months earlier after stints at Nice, OM and Air Bel. Author of three goals and an assist during the World Cup, the native of Neuilly-sur-Seine played his first (and only to date) Serie A match a few weeks later with the Italian club. Tracked by Brest in January, he finally chose to go on loan to Avellino, in Serie B, playing 11 matches. “Fabregas was completely in favor of my departure to Avellino. He told me it was the ideal place to continue my progress”he revealed.

This summer, it was with Hellas Verona, a club recently relegated to Serie B, that Andrea Le Borgne set down his bags. The former Nice player was able to meet several French people there, starting with the former PSG hopeful, Antoine Bernede, but also meeting Daniele Buzzegoli, assistant to coach Baroni whom he had known in the Como youth teams. Since his arrival, the former Lazio coach has made him one of his untouchables, and Le Borgne responds well to him on the pitch. Author of 2 assists, the Frenchman is considered one of the revelations of Serie B, despite a mixed start to the collective season (Hellas Verona are 9th but are only one point behind the first jump-off for the climb).

“Le Borgne establishes himself as a safe bet unlike other more experienced players. He is THE real revelation of the season for Hellas, and one of the most promising recruits. Its value quickly rose to 4 million euros. A few months ago, he was looking for his feet between the Primavera and the professional world. Today, Verona benefits from a young player with immense potential.writes the local media Tggialloblu. His performances would also be carefully observed by Cesc Fabregas and by Como, where the midfielder is under contract until 2028. After Lucas Da Cunha and Jean Butez, who became French internationals under his orders, the Spanish coach has perhaps found the next Frenchman whom he will explode. If Hellas Verona has a purchase option of €2.5 million, Como has reserved the right to include a buyout clause of €3 million, aware of the potential of its player.

Before Gasperini, Roma changed managers four times in just two seasons (2023-2025): Mourinho, De Rossi, Juric, and Ranieri.

The Grugliasco-born coach is restoring a stability lost due to poor decisions and questionable evaluations.

The coach himself, who won a Scudetto with AC Milan in Italy before returning to Italy to coach Fiorentina after his stint in Arabia, admitted the club’s interest.

Stefano Pioli could have coached Roma. The former AC Milan coach spoke to Sky Sport about the Giallorossi’s interest: “There were times when everyone called me. Even Roma, but I had just received my contract with Al Nassr and I couldn’t break my word.”

#1489. Europe’s top 10 dribblers in 2026-27: Diomande chasing Mbappe & Yamal

Stars from Barcelona and Real Madrid are currently among those making up the elite of dribblers in Europe’s top five leagues so far.

Here are the 10 players who have completed the most dribbles across Europe’s five major leagues so far (Premier League, La Liga, Ligue 1, Serie A and Bundesliga) this season.

Note: if two players are tied on the number of dribbles completed, we’ve listed them in order of superior success rate.

Soule has been making a habit of featuring in these rankings ever since he first caught the eye as a youngster at Frosinone.

The Argentine has completed 22 dribbles in 10 Serie A appearances this season, successfully beating his man on almost 60% of his attempts.

He’s continuing to deliver the goods at Roma. Still only 23, too.

Doku has completed 24 of his 47 attempted dribbles in the Premier League this season, having played just 307 minutes.

He’s averaging over seven successful dribbles per 90 minutes. Nobody in this top 10 comes close to matching that rate. He takes someone on roughly once every six minutes.

Fresh from becoming the youngest Moroccan player ever to score at a World Cup, Yassine has been playing for Strasbourg.

The BlueCo-owned club have seen Yassine make an impressive start to the campaign, with the youngster continuing to catch the eye in Ligue 1.

Dribbling-wise, he is already up to 26 completed in nine appearances, having played fewer games than most on this list.

He’s attempted 62 dribbles altogether, with 36 unsuccessful efforts giving him a success rate of 41.9%.

Having come through the Malaga youth academy, Larrubia has established himself in the first team of his boyhood club.

Playing on the right wing, he’s made over 140 appearances for the club at the age of 24 and is now the starting choice for Juan Francisco Funes.

This season, he’s attempted 65 dribbles and completed 26 of them, giving him a pretty sketchy success rate of exactly 40%. He’s now seventh in Europe’s major leagues for successful dribbles, but no player has registered more unsuccessful attempts than his 39.

The Germany Under-21 international is catching the eye once again at RB Leipzig, having rejoined the Bundesliga club on another loan from Brighton.

Gruda has completed 26 dribbles in just six league appearances, despite playing only 383 minutes. That’s an average of one successful dribble every 15 minutes.

He’s also been remarkably efficient, completing 61.9% of his 42 attempted dribbles. He ranks second for success rate among the players in this top 10.

The player has already spoken of how Mourinho has given him the freedom to play where he wants, and so this season is looking a lot more like his first year in Spain when he scored 19 league goals.

His willingness to get forward has also been shown in his dribbling numbers, with Bellingham one of the only midfielders to make the list, having completed 29 in 11 appearances so far.

The England international has attempted 48 dribbles altogether, completing 60.4% of them.

Kvernadze is not a name too many of you will be familiar with, but he is currently proving Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is not the only Georgian winger to be excited about.

Kvernadze plays for Serie A club Frosinone and leads the division for dribbles completed.

His tally of 29 is better than stars at Inter, Roma and Como. The fact he is doing this for little old Frosinone makes it all the more impressive.

Madrid spent big on the 19-year-old winger this summer and they’ll be hoping he can continue to inject some pace and danger into their attack.

Most impressively, he’s only notched 20 unsuccessful dribbles from 51 attempted, giving him a success rate of 60.8%.

Vinicius Junior will have his work cut out to make it back into Jose Mourinho’s preferred XI, and with regular starts Diomande could soon find himself challenging for the top spot on this list.

Considering he is one of the quickest but also most technically gifted players in the world, it should come as little surprise that Mbappe is second on this list.

He has started the season in excellent form, scoring a hat-trick against Real Sociedad and following that up with eight more goals over his next eight games.

As for the dribbles, Mbappe is second behind only Yamal, with 35 completed in 11 appearances. His success rate was dented by Madrid’s shock 1-0 loss at Real Betis and 2-1 defeat at Atletico Madrid, but the overall picture is altogether rosier.

He’s attempted 66 dribbles altogether, completing just over half. That’s a considerable improvement on his final ranking of sixth last season, which would suggest a change in how Mourinho wants him to play compared to how he did under Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa.

Barcelona’s teenage wonderkid is leading the list, having completed a ridiculous 43 dribbles in his 11 games so far this season.

Yamal has attempted a staggering 80 dribbles altogether, comfortably more than any other player in Europe’s five major leagues. He’s successful just over half the time, averaging a completed dribble every 21 minutes.

Yamal was top of last year’s rankings and is on track to do it again. What a player. And still somehow a teenager.

Marten De Roon’s experience for a Champions League night at Old Trafford.

#1485. Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe to the Ballon d'Or by one of the smallest margins EVER: Full results are revealed after England captain's triumph

Published: 17:30 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 17:33 EDT, 30 October 2026

Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe by a slender 28 point margin to be crowned as winner of the Ballon d'Or.

Kane claimed football's ultimate individual honour on Monday night, becoming the first Englishman to win since Michael Owen in 2001.

His success came off the back of a stunning year with Bayern Munich and England, with the forward netting a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season.

Kane's goals spearheaded Bayern Munich's domestic Treble, while he also captained England to third place at the World Cup.

A full breakdown of the results has now been revealed, with Kane topping the vote by receiving 1,055 points from an international jury of 100 journalists.

Mbappe, who had also been seeking to win the award for the first time in his career, finished agonisingly short with the Real Madrid and France star receiving 1,027.

Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by just a 28-point margin, the full vote breakdown has revealed

Kylian Mbappe narrowly missed out on winning the award for the first time in his career

The gap is shorter than the closely fought battle between Rodri and Vinicius Jr in 2024, with the Spaniard having triumphed on that occasion by just 41 points.

Lionel Messi's 2019 triumph over Virgil van Dijk is the narrowest margin of recent votes, with just seven points separating the pair.

Previously Matthias Sammer beat legendary Brazilian forward Ronaldo to the honour in 1996 by one point, with the same margin also seeing Sir Bobby Charlton beating Eusebio in 1966, when just 22 people voted.

In total, 40 of the voters had ranked Kane as their top choice, earning him 15 points each time, with Mbappe receiving 23 first place votes by comparison.

Kane was left out of the top ten by two journalists, while three overlooked Mbappe.

Lamine Yamal, who was widely viewed as a front-runner for the award alongside Kane and Mbappe, ultimately ended 174 points behind the winner.

Rodri and Messi completed the top five having earned 726 and 612 points respectively.

Since 2022, the current system is based on voting by a large panel of international journalists from the top 100 FIFA-ranked countries, and top 50 for the Ballon d'Or Feminin. Only a single journalist from each country in these rankings is given a vote.

Lamine Yamal ultimately ended in third place in the vote, finishing 174 points behind Kane

Kane and his wife Kate Goodland shared a kiss after he won the striker award (left) and Ballon d'Or (right) on Monday night

Each journalist must establish a ranking of top ten players from a list of 30 named players also designated by France Football.

A first place vote is worth 15 points, with the number reducing until tenth position, where players secure one point.

Voters are asked to take into account individual performances and their decisive and impressive character.

They are then requested to consider their collective role and the trophies won, before weighing up a player's class and fair play.

Kane had celebrated on Monday night with friends and family, including his wife Kate, after receiving the award at the London Palladium.

Kane made sure to pay tribute to Kate, who he married in 2019, after seeing off competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to win.

He said: 'To my wife, Kate, my best friend. We've been through ups and downs for sure. You're my biggest supporter. I actually felt like you wanted this more than me myself.

'The anxious wait for us to find out, I know it's been horrible for you, here it is - we've done it! You always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams, and I know they're your dreams as well, so it wouldn't be possible without you.

'This is a trophy that we celebrate, not me. This is me and you, it's all the family, all our close-knit team, so I just want to say thank you, I love you.

'Can't wait to enjoy this and celebrate tonight for sure. Love you.'

The couple share two daughters, Ivy and Vivienne, and two sons, Louis and Henry.

And Kane also made sure to reference them in his acceptance speech at the glitzy ceremony at the London Palladium.

'My kids sat home watching, it's definitely past your bedtime, especially as we're [the ceremony] a little later than we hoped,' he said. 'So to Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

'I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you.

'I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.'

The couple are both from Walthamstow and Kate has been the rock by her husband's side for years.

Kate is a sports science graduate and professional fitness coach, with 382k followers on Instagram.

The couple posed for photos on the red carpet at the London Palladium Theatre

Kane proposed in the Bahamas in 2017 and they married two years later, now living happily in Bavaria where they have settled well since the striker elevated his game to another level, dominating the Bundesliga.

During his emotional address on stage, he also thanked his parents. He said: 'Wow, wow, wow. I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. Made it a good omen for me tonight.

'Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was tough this year. Mum and dad, what a moment. All those years, the sacrifice, the support you gave me. Taking me to training, coming to watch me play. No matter where it was, even to this day you're there.

'All those traits you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight.'

And Kane got royal approval as he hit the summit of world football's personal awards from Prince William.

'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or!' William wrote in a post on Instagram. 'What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'

#1484. The 10 highest-scoring Englishmen for a foreign club as Bellingham scores 50th for Real Madrid

Jude Bellingham scored his 50th Real Madrid goal and, in doing so, moved one away from equalling Gary Lineker for the sixth most goals by an Englishman for a foreign club.

Real Madrid made light work of Racing Santander to earn a 3-0 win away from home and keep the pressure on leaders Barcelona.

Kylian Mbappe scored, because of course he did, before Bellingham got his fourth goal of the season.

On the break, Bellingham was played in by Mbappe before taking it round the keeper and sliding it into the empty net.

In doing so, Bellingham notched up 50 goals for Madrid, which is the sixth most for an Englishman for a foreign club.

Bellingham has 50 in 154 games, which is one shy of the 51 Gary Lineker scored for Barcelona. Although the former Match of the Day presenter managed his in 138 games.

There are no prizes for guessing who tops the list, with freshly minted Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane having scored 156 goals for Bayern Munich in 160 matches, while Jadon Sancho is third with 52 in 158 Dortmund games.

Rob McDonald, who played 115 games for Dutch side Groningen in the ’80s, is fourth with 52 goals.

With Lineker, McDonald and Sancho within reach, Bellingham should soon be third on this list, but he has some way to go to reach the 74 goals scored by David Loggie.

The striker, who played his football between 1975 and 1993, scored 74 goals for AZ Alkmaar in a six-year stint at the club.

Elsewhere on the list, Kevin Keegan is in 10th position for his 40 goals in 113 games, a period which also saw him win two Ballons d’Or.

Ray Clarke scored 41 goals for Sparta Rotterdam in the ‘70s and was most recently head scout at Blackburn Rovers.

Tony Woodcock scored 46 goals in 155 games for Koln, following successful stints at both Nottingham Forest and Arsenal. The Nottingham-born forward left Koln to join Arsenal, only to return for a second stint four years later.

Mason Greenwood scored 48 goals in 81 games for Marseille.

If you were to expand this list to include British players, John Charles and Gareth Bale would make the top 10.

Both Welshmen, Charles scored 105 goals in 182 games for Juventus while Bale netted 106 goals in 258 games for Real Madrid.

#1482. Which former footballers have run a marathon quicker than James Milner’s 3:09 in NYC?

Former Leeds United, Manchester City and Liverpool midfielder James Milner has added another remarkable achievement to his CV, completing the 2026 New York City Marathon in a seriously impressive time.

The former England international has always been something of a fitness fanatic, maintaining extraordinary standards throughout a career that saw him clock up more Premier League appearances than anyone else.

But where does his reported time of 3:09:04 put him among the quickest marathon-running footballers? We’ve compiled a list of 32 former professionals who’ve taken on the challenge, with some unexpected names making the cut.

Among those in the list are Champions League winners, Premier League stalwarts and some of the biggest names in European football. But the fastest is a legendary figure who has since become one of the world’s leading managers.

Credit to Famous PRs for compiling the data:

32. Leonardo Bonucci – London Marathon 2025 – 5:02:09| 31. John Terry – London Marathon 2025 – 5:00:43 30. Jody Morris – London Marathon 2025 – 5:00:43 29. Dejon Noel-Williams – London Marathon 2026 – 4:56:11 28. Mark Bright – London Marathon 2007 – 4:55:1727. 27. Steve Sidwell – London Marathon 2025 – 4:50:28 26. Lee Hendrie – London Marathon 2015 – 4:43:45 25. Felix Kroos – Berlin Marathon 2025 – 4:28:23 24. Edwin van der Sar – New York City Marathon 2011 – 4:19:16 23. Stephen Warnock – Virtual London Marathon 2020 – 4:17:09 22. Quinton Fortune – London Marathon 2017 – 4:06:29 21. Giuseppe Bergomi – New York City Marathon 2009 – 3:59:35 20. Lee Young-pyo – Seoul Marathon 2024 – 3:57:11 19. Tsuyoshi Kitazawa – Tokyo Marathon 2017 – 3:52:31 18. Pavel Nedved – Prague Marathon 2012 – 3:49:51 17. Gary Speed – London Marathon 2010 – 3:49:22 16. Michael Owen – London Marathon 2014 – 3:45:43 15. Kevin Kilbane – London Marathon 2015 – 3:38:58 14. Gary Rowett – London Marathon 2025 – 3:38:38 13. Kaka – Berlin Marathon 2022 – 3:38:06 12. Dwight Yorke – London Marathon 2011 – 3:31:56 11. Diego Ribas – Berlin Marathon 2025 – 3:31:52 10. Raul – New York City Marathon 2016 – 3:26:05 9. Andre Schurrle – Berlin Marathon 2025 – 3:21:25 8. Alvaro Arbeloa – Valencia Marathon 2019 – 3:15:21 7. Danny Mills – London Marathon 2023 – 3:12:18 6. James Milner – New York City Marathon 2026 – 3:09:04

So Milner’s time puts him above some pretty distinguished company, but there are five former footballers who have managed to go quicker.

The remaining five have all posted times that would be the envy of most amateur runners, with two even managing to break the elusive three-hour mark. There’s very little to separate the top four:

Not trying to step on Football Cliches‘ turf, but Christian Dailly is the name of a long-distance Olympian, not a Barclays-era stalwart. So this makes sense.

The former Scotland international had called time on a 22-year playing career in 2012, but wasn’t quite ready to put his sporting ambitions to bed. Instead, he turned his attention to athletics, becoming a coach and studying sports science at Manchester Metropolitan University.

In an interview with The Scotsman ahead of his first London Marathon in 2013, Dailly explained that he was more naturally suited to shorter, sharper events such as the 800m. He nevertheless had his sights set on a sub-three-hour marathon.

“You’re talking about someone who has had 22 years of football training and seven knee operations,” he said.

He ultimately finished in 3:06:26, just over six minutes outside his target. Not bad for a first attempt

You wouldn’t necessarily associate Grant with long-distance running, given he spent much of his career as a back-up, or latterly third-choice at Manchester United.

More accustomed to warming the bench than pounding the pavements? Apparently not.

Finishing just 33 seconds off the hallowed sub-three hours must’ve been a sickener, but at least he could console himself by comfortably beating Daddy Pig (5:51:53), Joe Wicks (5:51:54) and fellow journeyman keeper Darren Randolph (7:36:27).

A particularly impressive effort given the injury troubles that dogged his playing career. Ramsey completed the London Marathon in 3:00:30, three seconds quicker than Grant.

Only three celebrities went quicker: former Olympic cyclist Chris Newton (2:34:42), boxing trainer Shane McGuigan (2:44:51) and four-time F1 world champion Sebastian Vettel (2:59:08).

Ramsey retired from football the same month, aged 35, after a trophy-laden career with Arsenal, Juventus and Wales. He went straight into coaching, and is currently serving as the head coach of League One side Oxford United.

Dailly has the name of a marathon runner, Robben has the physique of one. He’s looked like a distance runner throughout his life, but even he admitted that 26.2 miles is a different proposition than sprinting up and down the wing.

“I am really broken, but I made it,” he told NOS after making the finish line.

“For a sprinter like me, such a distance is very long. But I love sports and I love a challenge.”

He had been training alongside former Dutch speed skater Erben Wennemars, who doubled up as his unofficial running coach and sports psychologist.

“Wennemars always says: once an athlete, always an athlete,” he added.

“I am no longer a top athlete, but I can tell you; I think it is elite sport if you can run a marathon in three hours.

“This comes very close to winning a great football title. Now I can check this off. I’m really happy.”

There are people who enjoy keeping fit, and then there’s Luis Enrique. The PSG manager is an absolute endurance nut, seemingly incapable of encountering a physical challenge without wanting to go all-in. Long-distance cycling is a particular passion, but he’s not afraid of mixing things up.

He competed in the notorious Marathon des Sables in 2008, running 155km across the Sahara over six days, and has also completed the Frankfurt Ironman: a 3.8km swim, 189km cycle and 42.2km marathon.

You’d imagine a sub-three-hour marathon barely registers on Luis Enrique’s personal difficulty scale. We’d have been disappointed if he hadn’t topped this particular leaderboard.

It’s an attitude that carries over into his coaching. Luis Enrique is famously demanding, expecting his players to push themselves to their physical and mental limits. His PSG side have won back-to-back European titles by embodying precisely those principles, with every player expected to work hard, sacrifice and run their b*llocks off.

#1480. Sportword: Play daily football word game on Planet Sport

Sportword is Planet Sport’s game which challenges you to guess football and other sport-related words within six attempts.

As you might have guessed, it’s the football version we’re hosting here on Planet Football, adding to our hundreds of other football quizzes many of you already play daily, including our type-in-the-answer list quizzes and our complete-the-football-line-up quizzes.

We are busy building a new home for Sportword and all our other sport games and quizzes, but in the meantime, you can play the daily football game right here so please bookmark this page, try today’s word and then come back tomorrow.

Simply put, you have six attempts to guess a word. There will be a clue for each one to focus your mind a little.

Type in your first guess then hit enter. Each tile will change colour to indicate if the letter is in the correct position, elsewhere in the word or does not appear at all. A green tile means the letter is in the correct position; an orange tile means the letter is elsewhere in the word; a grey tile means that letter is not in the word at all.

If you are struggling, you will see a hint button that becomes available from your fourth attempt. Clicking it will reveal a tile, though note this is only available to logged-in users.

You can also click Give Up if you’re really struggling and just want to be put out of your misery. It’s not one for the purists, but it’s nice to have the option!

As with all our other football quizzes, we also have a leaderboard that ranks players by the number of attempts and time they required to guess the correct word.

F1 fans can play the daily F1 Sportword game over on PlanetF1. We will be launching rugby, rugby league and tennis versions in the future too, and in our soon-to-launch games hub you’ll be able to play sub-categories, for example 2000s Premier League players.
